hints.content:
Let's draw a line $\ell$ and a point $A$ on that line.


[[☃ image 1]]

Then we can draw several random points, perform the transformation, and see what happens!

options.alt: A vertical line l. Point A is directly on the line. Point P is at the top to the right of the line. Point Q is on the left side of the line close to the middle of it. Point R is on the right side of the line at the bottom.

hints.content:
[[☃ image 1]]

Each point maps to the other side of $\ell$ and remains the same distance from $\ell$. Also, the segments between each pre-image and image are perpendicular to $\ell$. Therefore, this transformation is a reflection.

options.alt: A vertical line l. Point A is directly on the line. Point P is at the top to the right of the line. Point Q is on the left side of the line close to the middle of it. Point R is on the right side of the line at the bottom. Points P, Q, and R are reflected across the vertical line l. Point P prime is the same distance from the line a point P but on the left side of the line. Point A prime is on point A. Point Q prime is on the opposite side with the same distance away from the vertical line as point Q. Point Q prime is on the opposite side with the same distance away from the vertical line as point R.

question.content:
A certain mapping in the $xy$-plane has the following properties:

- Every point $A$ on line $\ell$ maps to itself.
- Every point $P$ that isn't on $\ell$ maps to point $P'$ such that $\ell$ is the perpendicular bisector of $PP'$

**Which transformation does the mapping define?**
